477.title: DISC Child
477.description:
Safety Interventions Instructions for HEP

As a safety precaution, all participants who endorse current depression on the DISC must be referred for psychiatric evaluation. Please plan ahead for this possibility by creating a list of local mental health providers to be given to participants if needed.

Participants who are found to have a lifetime history of major depression on the DISC (MDD section) and who answer question 14 as their current age will be referred for psychiatric treatment.

With all psychiatric referrals, the phenotyping clinician should explain to the participant that the interview suggests that they should seek evaluation by a mental health provider; please emphasize that this is not a clinical diagnosis. The participant’s parent or guardian must also be notified immediately of any psychiatric diagnoses, including if the parent/guardian is not present during the C-SSRS administration. Lastly, please also ask for written permission from the participant and/or parent or guardian to contact their primary care provider and notify them of the participant’s DISC score indicative of depression.

After completion of the study visit:
- fill out the HEP Safety Intervention Form in REDCap, and
- follow up with the participant 1 week after referral to confirm they were able to schedule an appointment with a mental health provider.

If you have any questions or concerns as to a participant's diagnosis, please contact Dr. Andres Kanner at 847-476-1811 (or if Dr. Kanner is unavailable, Dr. Siddhartha Nadkarni at 917-763-1016).

To be administered to children ages seven and older for those diagnoses not present or “subthreshold” in current state.

Note: “Subthreshold” means that impairment and onset questions for the diagnosis were asked.

1.1.field_description:
The questions I will ask you are about problems you may have had in the past or may have now. I want you to think
about the whole time since you turned 5 years old.

1.3.field_title: 1. Since you turned five years old, has there ever been a period of time when you worried too much about  a number of different things ... maybe things like whether you would make good grades in school ... or  how you would do in sports ... or that you might have some sickness or illness?

1.4.field_title: IF NO, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.5.field_title: 1A. Did your worrying too much about things go on for a long time, at least for several months in a row?

1.6.field_title: IF NO, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.7.field_title: 1B. Was it very hard for you to stop yourself from worrying about these things?

1.8.field_title: IF NO, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.9.field_title: 2. How old were you when you first started to worry so much? (Years)

1.11.field_title: IF AGE NOT KNOWN, ASK: What grade were you in?

1.13.field_title: 3. How old were you when you stopped worrying that much? CODE AGE (00 = IN LAST 12 MONTHS, 88 = NEVER STOPPED)

1.15.field_title: IF AGE NOT KNOWN, ASK: What grade were you in?

1.17.field_title: 4. Now I want to ask you some questions about the time you worried so much [between the ages of ____ and ____/when you were ____/when you were in ____ grade(s)]. Did worrying so much make it hard for you to keep your mind on other things?

1.19.field_title: 5. When you were worried like that, did you feel also tense, restless, or tired out?

1.21.field_title: 6. When you were worried like that, were you grouchy or irritable a lot of the time?

1.23.field_title: 7. Did worrying so much interfere with your sleep?

1.24.field_title: 8. Did worrying like that give you headaches or other aches and pains?

1.25.field_title: 9. Did worrying like that make you get tired very easily?

1.26.field_title: 10. Did worrying so much cause any serious problems for you at home, (at school) or with your friends?

1.27.field_title: 11. Did you ever see a doctor, counselor, or some other person like that because you worried too much?

1.28.field_title: 12. Did worrying a lot make you feel really unhappy or bother you a lot?

1.30.field_title: 1. Since you turned five years old, was there a time when you were nervous or uncomfortable almost every time you had to talk to people you didn't know well?

1.31.field_title: 2. Since you turned five years old, was there a time when you were very nervous or uncomfortable almost every time you had to do something when other people were looking at you ... like speaking in front of the class ... or eating where other people could see you - like in the school lunchroom or at a restaurant?

1.32.field_title: IF ANY RESPONSES WERE CODED "YES" IN Q 1 - 2, CONTINUE. ALL OTHERS, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.33.field_title: 3. Now I want you to think about the reason you felt nervous or uncomfortable about [talking to people you didn't know well/doing something when other people were looking at you]. Was it because you thought you would embarrass yourself or make a fool of yourself?

1.34.field_title: 4. Did your being nervous or uncomfortable whenever you [talked to people you didn't know well/did something when other people were looking at you] last several months in a row?

1.35.field_title: IF NO, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.36.field_title: 5. How old were you when you first started being afraid of [talking to people you didn't know well/doing something when other people were looking at you]?

1.38.field_title: IF AGE NOT KNOWN, ASK: What grade were you in?

1.40.field_title: 6. How old were you when you last were afraid of [talking to people you didn't know well/doing something when other people were looking at you]? CODE AGE (00 = IN LAST 12 MONTHS, 88 = NEVER STOPPED)

1.42.field_title: IF AGE NOT KNOWN, ASK: What grade were you in?

1.44.field_title: 7. Now I want to ask you some questions about other things that were going on [between the ages of ____ and ____/when you were ____/when you were in ____ grade(s)]. During that time, did you have friends your age who you liked spending time with?

1.45.field_title: 8. Did being nervous or uncomfortable when you [talked to people you didn't know well/did something when other people were looking at you] cause any serious problems for you at home, (at school) or with your friends?

1.46.field_title: 9. Did you ever see a doctor, counselor, or some other person like that because you were nervous or uncomfortable when you [talked to people you didn't know well/did something when other people were looking at you]?

1.47.field_title: 10. Did being nervous or uncomfortable when you [talked to people you didn't know well/did something when other people were looking at you] make you feel really unhappy or bother you a lot?

1.49.field_title: Since you turned five years old, has there been a time when you were almost always very, very afraid of:

1.50.field_title: 1. Dogs, birds, snakes, insects, or any other animals?

1.51.field_title: 2. How about being really afraid of being up high or in a high place?

1.52.field_title: 3. How about being really afraid of thunder and lightening?

1.53.field_title: 4. ... or being afraid of the dark?

1.54.field_title: 5. Were you very afraid of water, like a pool or a lake?

1.55.field_title: 6. ... or being on a bridge ... or in a tunnel ... or on a highway?

1.56.field_title: 7. Were you really afraid of elevators or escalators?

1.57.field_title: 8. Were you very afraid of needles or shots?

1.58.field_title: 9. Were you really afraid to see blood or to see someone with a bad cut?

1.59.field_title: IF A "YES" RESPONSE WAS CODED IN Q 1 - 9, CONTINUE. ALL OTHERS, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.60.field_title: 10. You said you were afraid of [NAME SPECIFIC FEAR(S)]. Were you afraid of [[NAME SPECIFIC FEAR]/any of those things] for several months in a row or longer?

1.61.field_title: IF MORE THAN ONE FEAR, ASK 10 A, ALL OTHERS, GO TO Q 11

1.62.field_title: 10 A. Which one(s) were you afraid of for several months or longer?

1.63.field_title: 11. How old were you when you first started to be afraid of (any of) [NAME FEAR(S)]?

1.65.field_title: IF AGE NOT KNOWN, ASK: What grade were you in?

1.67.field_title: 12. How old were you when you became less afraid of [NAME FEAR(S)]? CODE AGE (00 = IN LAST 12 MONTHS, 88 = NEVER STOPPED)

1.69.field_title: IF AGE NOT KNOWN, ASK: What grade were you in?

1.71.field_title: 13. Now I want to ask you some questions about the time you were afraid of [NAME FEAR(S)] [between ages ____ and ____/when you were ____/when you were in ____ grade(s)]. When you were around [NAME FEAR(S)], did [it/they] nearly always make you feel really upset?

1.72.field_title: 14. Were you so afraid of [NAME FEAR(S)] that you tried to stay away from [them/it]?

1.73.field_title: 14a. If you couldn't stay away from [them/it], did you feel afraid the whole time you were there?

1.74.field_title: IF A 'YES' RESPONSE WAS CODED IN Q 14 OR 14A, CONTINUE. ALL OTHERS, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.75.field_title: 15. Did being afraid like that cause any big problems for you at home, (at school) or with your friends?

1.76.field_title: 16. Did you ever see a doctor, counselor, or some other person like that because you were afraid of [NAME FEAR(S)]?

1.77.field_title: 17. Did being afraid of [NAME FEAR(S)] make you feel really unhappy or bother you a lot?

1.79.field_title: 1. Since you turned five years old, was there ever a time when you had a sudden attack of feeling very scared and strange things would happen to you, all at once ... things like you couldn't catch your breath ... or you felt like you were choking ... or your heart started beating really fast ... or your chest hurt ... or you felt dizzy ... or you felt very hot or cold ... or you felt like you were going to die or go crazy?

1.80.field_title: 1A. Would you have two or more of these feelings at the same time?

1.81.field_title: IF NO, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.82.field_title: 1B. Would several of these feelings start within the same few minutes, like an attack?

1.83.field_title: IF NO, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.84.field_title: 1C. Have you had more than one attack like this?

1.85.field_title: IF NO, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.86.field_title: 1D. Did these attacks ever come on when you didn't expect them?

1.87.field_title: 2. How old were you when you first had one of these attacks? (years)

1.89.field_title: IF AGE NOT KNOWN, ASK: What grade were you in?

1.91.field_title: 3. How old were you the last time you had one of these attacks?

1.93.field_title: IF AGE NOT KNOWN, ASK: What grade were you in?

1.95.field_title: 4. Now I want to ask you some questions about the time you were having these attacks [between the ages of ____ and ____/when you were ____/when you were in ____ grade(s)]. After you had an attack, did you worry a lot that it might happen again?

1.96.field_title: 4A. Did you worry that having these attacks meant there was something really wrong with you?

1.97.field_title: 4B. Did you stop doing things you liked because you thought you might have an attack if you did them?

1.98.field_title: 4C. Did you stop going places where you might not be able to get help if you had an attack?

1.99.field_title: 5. Did having these attacks cause any serious problems for you at home, (at school) or with your friends?

1.100.field_title: 6. Did you ever see a doctor, counselor, or some other person like that about these attacks?

1.101.field_title: 7. Did having these attacks make you feel really unhappy or bother you a lot?

1.103.field_title: 1. I'll be asking you next about whether you ever have had a couple of weeks or more when you felt depressed or sad most of the time or felt like you didn't enjoy things. I don't mean just ordinary sadness; I mean a couple of weeks when nearly all the time you felt really sad or miserable ... or when you just couldn't seem to enjoy anything as much as usual ... or nothing you did seemed fun ... or when you were so irritable or grouchy that everything got on your nerves. Since you turned five years old, have you felt like that almost everyday for a couple of weeks in a row?

1.104.field_title: 2. Which of the feelings I mentioned did you have at that time? That is, did you feel sad all day long?

1.105.field_title: 3. Did it feel like you couldn't enjoy anything or that nothing seemed fun?

1.106.field_title: 4. Did you feel really grouchy or irritable almost everyday?

1.107.field_title: NOTE 2: Was a 'YES' response coded in Q2 or Q4?

1.108.field_title: IF A 'YES' RESPONSE W0AS CODED IN Q 2 - 4, CONTINUE AND USE FIRST 'YES' 'MOOD' AS KEYWORD IN Q 5 - 20. ALL OTHERS, GO TO NEXT DIAGNOSIS

1.109.field_title: 5. Now I want to ask you some questions about the time you were [sad/not able to enjoy things/grouchy or irritable]. When you were [sad/not able to enjoy things/grouchy or irritable], was it hard for you to keep your mind on what you were doing, to think clearly, or to make up your mind about even little things?

1.110.field_title: 6. When you were [sad/not able to enjoy things/grouchy or irritable], did you feel that you were "no good," or did you blame yourself for all sorts of things?

1.111.field_title: 7. When you were [sad/not able to enjoy things/grouchy or irritable], did your eating change ... for example, did you eat much less than usual ... or did you eat a whole lot more than usual?

1.112.field_title: 8. Did you feel really tired all the time, or did you have so little energy that it took a big effort to do anything?

1.113.field_title: IF 5 OR MORE 'YES' RESPONSES WERE CODED IN Q 3-8 AND NOTE 2, GO TO Q 13

1.114.field_title: 9. When you were [sad/not able to enjoy things/grouchy or irritable], did your sleeping change so that you wanted to sleep all the time, or so that you had trouble with falling asleep or staying asleep?

1.140.field_title: 1. Now I want to ask about a time when other people were worried about you because you were getting too excited or happy, so excited or happy that nothing could calm you down. I don’t mean just being happy or excited because something really special was happening. I am talking about a real change from how you usually are, when there was nothing special going on … a change that lasted for several days, and made other people worry about you. Since you turned five years old, have you ever had a time like that?

1.141.field_title: Q1A. Was there at least a whole week when you felt too happy or excited almost all the time?

1.142.field_title: Q1B. Did you have to go to the hospital because you or other people were worried about the way you were acting?

Have you ever had a week or more when you felt as grouchy or irritable as that?
